lessons.title: 5.5 Transversals and 5.6 Corresponding Angles

activities.prompt: How can one angle reveal whether two lines are parallel?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet Transversals
activities.body: A transversal intersects two different lines and forms eight angles. One line gets one angle set, and the other gets another. These angles make four vertically opposite pairs. Each pair has equal angles. There are at most four different measures. Corresponding pairs include 1 and 5. Also, 2 and 6, 3 and 7, and 4 and 8 are corresponding pairs. Equal corresponding angles show that the lines are parallel.
keyPoints: A transversal intersects two different lines.
The eight angles make four vertically opposite pairs.
Equal corresponding angles show that the lines are parallel.
activities.explanation: These are the main ideas for transversals and corresponding angles.

activities.title: The Corresponding-Angle Rule
activities.body: Equal corresponding angles give a clear clue about two lines. If the angles are equal, the lines are parallel. The reverse also holds: across parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal. Across lines that are not parallel, corresponding angles cannot be equal. You can use these ideas as a treasure guide. Look at a pair, compare its measures, then decide whether the lines are parallel.
keyPoints: Equal corresponding angles show parallel lines.
Corresponding angles are equal across parallel lines.
They cannot be equal across non-parallel lines.
activities.explanation: These ideas show both directions of the corresponding-angle rule.

activities.prompt: Which description matches a transversal?
activities.explanation: A transversal is a line that intersects two different lines.

activities.prompt: Match each corresponding pair with its second angle.
activities.explanation: Each listed pair is a corresponding pair in the lesson.

activities.prompt: If one angle is 60 degrees, its linear pair is ______ degrees.
activities.hint: Use the linear pair example in your lesson.
activities.explanation: The angle in this linear pair measures 120 degrees.

activities.prompt: At one road crossing, one angle is 30 degrees. What is the measure of its vertically opposite angle in degrees?
activities.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the other angle is a degrees.

activities.prompt: Put these steps for proving parallel lines in order.
items: Confirm that the pair is equal
Conclude that the lines are parallel
activities.explanation: Equal corresponding angles let you show that the lines are parallel.

activities.prompt: A bus route crosses two parallel roads. Angle 1 is 35 degrees. What is the measure of angle 5 in degrees?
activities.explanation: Angles 1 and 5 are corresponding angles. Corresponding angles formed across parallel lines are equal, so angle 5 is a degrees.

activities.prompt: A bus route crosses two non-parallel roads. The larger corresponding angle is 70 degrees and the smaller is 50 degrees. What is their difference in degrees?
activities.explanation: Corresponding angles across non-parallel lines cannot be equal. Their difference is a - b degrees.

activities.prompt: One angle in a linear pair is 60 degrees. What is the measure of the other angle in the linear pair in degrees?
activities.explanation: The two angles in a linear pair add to 180 degrees, so the other angle is 180 - a degrees.

lessons.title: 5.7 Drawing Parallel Lines

activities.prompt: How can we draw a perfect pair of parallel lines?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How to Draw Parallel Lines
activities.body: Slide a set square along a scale line to draw two perpendicular lines. Perpendicular means at a right angle. Each angle with the scale line measures 90 degrees. Matching angles are called corresponding angles. Equal corresponding angles show that the two new lines are parallel. For paper folding, first fold a perpendicular to line l through point A. Then fold another perpendicular through point A. The final crease m is parallel to line l.
keyPoints: Sliding a set square can draw perpendicular lines.
Equal corresponding angles show that lines are parallel.
The final crease m is parallel to line l.
activities.explanation: These methods use right angles and equal corresponding angles.

activities.title: Sliding a Set Square
activities.prompt: Sliding a set square along a scale can draw two perpendicular lines.
activities.explanation: Yes. Both new lines can be perpendicular to the scale line.

activities.title: Angles with the Scale Line
activities.prompt: What do the angles made with the scale line measure?
options: The two angles have different sizes.
The angles are parallel to each other.
The angles change while you slide.
activities.explanation: Each angle with the scale line measures 90 degrees.

activities.prompt: A carpenter slides a set square along a scale line and makes 1 perpendicular line at one mark and 1 perpendicular line at another mark. How many perpendicular lines are made in total?
activities.explanation: One line is made at each mark, so the total is 1 + 1 = 2 lines.

activities.prompt: Two new lines are perpendicular to a scale line. Their angles with the scale line are 90 and 90 degrees. What is the sum of the two angles in degrees?
activities.explanation: Each angle is a right angle, so their sum is 90 + 90 = 180 degrees.

activities.prompt: Line l crosses two new lines. Two corresponding angles are 90 and 90 degrees. What is the sum of these corresponding angles in degrees?
activities.explanation: Each corresponding angle is 90 degrees, so the sum is 90 + 90 = 180 degrees.

activities.title: Match the Ideas
activities.prompt: Match each part of the lesson to its result.
pairs: long side of a set square
activities.explanation: Equal corresponding angles help you identify parallel lines.

activities.title: Paper-Folding Order
activities.prompt: Put the paper-folding instructions and result in order.
items: First, fold a perpendicular to line l through point A.
Then, fold a perpendicular to the new crease through point A.
The final crease m is parallel to line l.
activities.explanation: The two folds create crease m, which is parallel to line l.

activities.prompt: For folding a paper strip, Riya first folds a line through point A perpendicular to line l. What angle does this first crease make with line l in degrees?
activities.explanation: A perpendicular line makes a right angle with line l, so the angle is 90 degrees.

lessons.title: 5.8 Alternate Angles and 5.9 Parallel Illusions

activities.prompt: Could two straight lines really hide a pair of matching angles?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Alternate Angles
activities.body: Alternate angles across parallel lines are always equal. The matching angle for f is b. It is the corresponding angle. Angle d is vertically opposite b, directly across from it. Angle d is the alternate angle of f. Angles 3 and 6 are interior. Interior angles on one side of the crossing line add to 180 degrees. Angles 5 and 6 form a linear pair and measure 180 degrees together.
keyPoints: Alternate angles across parallel lines are always equal.
Angle b and d have equal measures. Angle d is f's alternate angle.
Interior angles on one side of the crossing line add to 180 degrees.
activities.explanation: Use equal angles and parallel lines to find hidden angle relationships.

activities.prompt: Which angle is the alternate angle of angle f?
activities.explanation: Angle d is the alternate angle of angle f.

activities.prompt: Angle f measures 120 degrees. What does angle d measure?
activities.explanation: Angle d is f's alternate angle, so both measure 120 degrees.

activities.prompt: Match each angle or group with its relationship.
activities.explanation: These pairs use the alternate, vertical, corresponding, interior, and linear-pair relationships.

activities.prompt: Angle f measures 60°. What does its alternate angle d measure in degrees?
activities.explanation: Alternate angles have equal measures, so angle d = angle f = 60°. The answer is 60°.

activities.prompt: Angle f measures 135°. What does its corresponding angle b measure in degrees?
activities.explanation: A corresponding angle has the same measure, so angle b = angle f = 135°. The answer is 135°.

activities.prompt: Angle b measures 60°. What does its vertically opposite angle d measure in degrees?
activities.explanation: Vertically opposite angles have equal measures, so angle d = angle b = 60°. The answer is 60°.

activities.prompt: A bus route crosses two parallel roads. Angle d measures 120°. What does alternate angle f measure in degrees?
activities.explanation: Alternate angles formed across parallel lines are equal, so angle f = angle d = 120°. The answer is 120°.

activities.prompt: Angles 5 and 6 form a linear pair in a road drawing. Angle 5 measures 60°. What does angle 6 measure in degrees?
activities.explanation: Angles in a linear pair add to 180°. Therefore, angle 6 = 180 - 60 = 120°.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to find the alternate angle of angle f.
items: Copy angle b's measure for angle f.
Match angle b's measure with vertically opposite angle d.
Use angle d as the alternate angle of f.
activities.explanation: Angle b and f have equal measures. Angle d is vertically opposite b and has the same measure. So d is f's alternate angle.

activities.prompt: Angle 2 measures 30°. It corresponds to angle 6. What does angle 6 measure in degrees?
activities.explanation: Corresponding angles have equal measures, so angle 6 = angle 2 = 30°. The answer is 30°.

lessons.title: Numbers Tell Us Things

activities.prompt: Can you uncover what each child’s number reveals about their height?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Numbers Describe an Arrangement
activities.body: In this lesson, each child says how many children in front are taller than them. Children 1, 2, 4 and 6 call out 0. Child 3 calls out 1. Children 5 and 7 call out 3. The largest possible number in a group of 8 people is 7. Numbers can show how a sequence is arranged without showing the actual numbers.
keyPoints: Each child counts taller children in front.
The called numbers describe the shown arrangement.
Numbers can describe an arrangement without showing the actual numbers.
activities.explanation: The calls help us understand how the children are arranged.

activities.title: Child 3's Call
activities.prompt: In the shown arrangement, what number does child 3 call out?
activities.explanation: Child 3 calls out 1. This is the number of taller children in front.

activities.title: Same Number
activities.prompt: Child 5 calls out the same number as child 7.
activities.explanation: Child 5 calls out 3. Child 7 also calls out 3.

activities.prompt: A group has 3 children. What is the largest possible number a child can call out, in children?
activities.explanation: The largest possible callout is n - 1 = 2 children.

activities.prompt: A child in a line calls out 2. How many taller children are in front of that child?
activities.explanation: The callout c counts exactly the taller children in front, so the answer is c children.

activities.prompt: In the shown arrangement, child 2 is in the line. How many children are in front of child 2?
activities.explanation: Before position i there are i - 1 = 1 children.

activities.prompt: A line has 6 children. Child 4 is in the line. How many children are behind child 4?
activities.explanation: There are n - i = 2 children behind child i.

activities.prompt: Child 5 calls out 0. Of the children in front, how many are not taller than this child?
activities.explanation: There are i - 1 children in front, and c of them are taller, so (i - 1) - c = 4 children are not taller.

activities.title: Order the Called Numbers
activities.prompt: Put these children in order from the smallest called number to the largest.
activities.explanation: Child 4 calls out 0. Child 3 calls out 1. Child 5 calls out 3.

activities.title: The Largest Possible Number
activities.prompt: What is the largest possible number in a group of 8 people?
activities.explanation: The largest possible number in a group of 8 people is 7.

activities.prompt: Two children in different lines call out 1 and 3. How many taller children do their callouts count altogether?
activities.explanation: Adding the two callouts gives x + y = 4 taller children altogether.

lessons.title: Even Numbers and Odd Numbers

activities.prompt: Ready to discover what makes a number even or odd?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Even Numbers and Odd Numbers
activities.body: Even numbers can be arranged in pairs without leftovers. Odd numbers cannot be arranged completely in pairs. An odd number is one more than a collection of pairs. Parity means being even or odd. The sum of two odd numbers is always even. The sum of three odd numbers cannot be arranged in pairs. Two consecutive numbers contain one even number and one odd number.
keyPoints: Even numbers can be arranged in pairs.
Odd numbers have one number left over.
Parity means being even or odd.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you spot even and odd numbers.

activities.prompt: Match each number idea to its meaning.
pairs: Can be arranged in pairs without leftovers
Cannot be arranged completely in pairs
The property of being even or odd
Contain one even number and one odd number
activities.explanation: Each idea has a clear meaning from this lesson.

activities.prompt: A tray has 14 laddoos. All the laddoos are arranged in pairs with none left over. How many pairs are there?
activities.explanation: Number of pairs = 14/2. For example, 8/2 = 4 pairs.

activities.prompt: A shop has 12 red pencils and 20 blue pencils. Both numbers are even. How many pencils are there in total?
activities.explanation: Total pencils = 12 + 20. For example, 10 + 8 = 18 pencils, and 18 is even.

activities.prompt: Ravi has 9 red marbles and 11 blue marbles. Both numbers are odd. How many marbles does he have in total?
activities.explanation: Total marbles = 9 + 11. For example, 5 + 3 = 8 marbles, and 8 is even.

activities.prompt: Three bags have 5, 11, and 15 laddoos. Each number is odd. How many laddoos are there in total?
activities.explanation: Total laddoos = 5 + 11 + 15. For example, 3 + 5 + 7 = 15 laddoos, which is odd and cannot be arranged completely in pairs.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to find what happens to two odd numbers.
activities.explanation: The sum of two odd numbers can always be arranged in pairs.

activities.prompt: What happens when you add 3 odd numbers?
options: The sum can be arranged in pairs
The sum cannot be arranged in pairs
activities.explanation: The sum of 3 odd numbers cannot be arranged in pairs.

activities.prompt: Adding any 5 odd numbers can give an even number.
activities.explanation: False. Adding any 5 odd numbers can never give an even number.

activities.prompt: Five trays have 3, 9, 19, 21, and 29 laddoos. Every number is odd. How many laddoos are there in total?
activities.explanation: Total laddoos = 3 + 9 + 19 + 21 + 29. For example, 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 35 laddoos, which is odd.

lessons.title: Parity in Grids and Expressions

activities.prompt: Can you discover what makes a number or grid odd or even?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Odd, Even and Parity
activities.body: A grid’s parity can be odd or even. A 3 × 3 grid has 9 small squares, so it is odd. A 3 × 4 grid has 12 small squares, so it is even. One even dimension makes a grid even. Both odd dimensions make it odd. The formulas 2n and 2n – 1 give the nth even and odd numbers. Also, 3n + 4 can have either parity.
keyPoints: A 3 × 3 grid is odd; a 3 × 4 grid is even.
One even dimension means an even grid.
2n gives the nth even number; 2n – 1 gives the nth odd number.
activities.explanation: Even and odd patterns follow clear rules.

activities.prompt: A 3 × 3 grid contains how many small squares, and what is its parity?
activities.explanation: The 3 × 3 grid has 9 small squares. Nine is odd.

activities.prompt: A 3 × 4 grid has 12 small squares, so its parity is even.
activities.explanation: The 3 × 4 grid has 12 small squares, so its parity is even.

activities.prompt: Which dimension pair gives an odd number of small squares?
activities.explanation: The rule says both dimensions must be odd for an odd grid.

activities.prompt: Match each expression or formula with its description.
pairs: does not list every even number
activities.explanation: Each pair matches a rule or description given in the lesson.

activities.prompt: The 100th even number is ______.
activities.explanation: The chapter says that the 100th even number is 200.

activities.prompt: Put these even numbers from smallest to largest.
activities.explanation: Using 2n gives 2, 4, 6 and 8 in order.

activities.prompt: What does the lesson say about 6k + 2?
options: It gives the nth even number.
It gives the nth odd number.

activities.prompt: What secret pattern could make a grid feel like magic?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What makes a magic square?
activities.body: Think of a grid as rows and columns. A magic square has the same sum in every row, column and diagonal. A diagonal joins opposite corners. The common sum is called the magic sum. For a square using 1 to 9, the magic sum is 15, and the centre is 5. The numbers 1 and 9 cannot sit in corners.
keyPoints: Rows, columns and diagonals have equal sums.
The common sum is called the magic sum.
A magic sum of 15 needs 5 in the centre.
activities.explanation: A magic square keeps equal sums in its rows, columns and diagonals.

activities.prompt: A magic square using 1 to 9 has a magic sum of ______.
activities.hint: Remember the special sum for this square.
activities.explanation: A magic square using 1 to 9 must have a magic sum of 15.

activities.prompt: Match each magic-square clue to its answer.

Sum of each Chautīsā Yantra line
Ways to fill a 3 × 3 grid with 1 to 9
Site of the first recorded 4 × 4 magic square
activities.explanation: Each clue matches the special value or place given in the lesson.

activities.prompt: A grid row has 7 marbles, 4 marbles, and 3 marbles. What does the circled number for this row show, in marbles?
activities.explanation: The circled number gives the sum of the row. Add all three marble counts.

activities.prompt: Three marbles carry different point labels from 1 to 9. The smallest possible labels are 1, 2, and 3. What is their total in points?
activities.explanation: The three smallest different numbers from 1 to 9 are 1, 2, and 3. Their sum is 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 points.

activities.prompt: Three marbles carry different point labels from 1 to 9. The largest possible labels are 7, 8, and 9. What is their total in points?
activities.explanation: The three largest different numbers from 1 to 9 are 7, 8, and 9. Their sum is 7 + 8 + 9 = 24 points.

activities.prompt: A 3 × 3 magic square uses 1 to 9. Its top row has 8, 1, and 6. What is its magic sum in points?
activities.explanation: A magic square has equal sums for its rows, columns, and diagonals. The common sum is called the magic sum, and here 8 + 1 + 6 = 15 points.

activities.prompt: The numbers 1 and 9 can appear in the corners of a 1-to-9 magic square.
activities.explanation: The numbers 1 and 9 cannot occur in corners of a 1-to-9 magic square.

activities.prompt: The first recorded 4 × 4 magic square was found in Khajuraho.
activities.explanation: It was found at the Pārśhvanath Jain temple in Khajuraho.

activities.prompt: A 3 × 3 magic square uses the number labels 1 to 9. What number label must be in its centre?
activities.explanation: The centre number of a magic square using 1 to 9 must be 5. Here, (1 + 9) / 2 = 5.

activities.prompt: A 3 × 3 magic square uses 9 different numbers from 1 to 9. The numbers 1 and 9 cannot be in corners. How many other numbers are not ruled out for a corner?
activities.explanation: There are 9 numbers altogether. Removing the two corner numbers, 1 and 9, leaves 9 - 1 - 1 = 7 numbers.

lessons.title: Virahāṅka–Fibonacci Numbers

activities.prompt: How did ancient poets help mathematicians find a special number pattern?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Numbers Connected with Poetry
activities.body: Virahāṅka numbers first appeared in work connected with poetry. In Sanskrit, Prakrit and other Indian poetry, each syllable is long or short. A short syllable lasts one beat. A long syllable lasts exactly twice as long, so it lasts two beats. Virahāṅka gave his counting method around 700 CE. Fibonacci wrote about these numbers in 1202 CE.
keyPoints: The numbers first appeared in work connected with poetry.
Short syllables last one beat, while long syllables last two.
Virahāṅka shared his method around 700 CE.
activities.explanation: You can see how poetry, counting and mathematics are closely linked.

activities.prompt: How many rhythms have 6 beats?
activities.explanation: There are 13 rhythms having 6 beats.

activities.prompt: Match each item with its time length or date.
activities.explanation: Each item is paired with its time length or date from the lesson.

activities.prompt: A poem has 5 short syllables and 2 long syllables. How many beats does the poem take?
activities.explanation: Each short syllable takes 1 beat and each long syllable takes 2 beats, so the total is s + 2*l beats. For example, s = 3 and l = 2 gives 3 + 2*2 = 7 beats.

activities.prompt: A poem has 1 rhythms, and each rhythm has 6 beats. How many beats are there in all?
activities.explanation: Multiply the number of rhythms by the beats in each rhythm: r*b beats. For example, r = 3 and b = 6 gives 3*6 = 18 beats.

activities.prompt: There are 8 rhythms with 5 beats and 8 rhythms with 6 beats. How many rhythms are there in all?
activities.explanation: Add the two groups of rhythms: a+b rhythms. For example, a = 8 and b = 13 gives 8+13 = 21 rhythms.

activities.prompt: One rhythm has 8 beats and another has 6 beats. What is the difference in their numbers of beats?
activities.explanation: Subtract the smaller number of beats from the larger number: 8-b beats. For example, b = 6 gives 8-6 = 2 beats.

activities.prompt: Piṅgala lived around 302 BCE and Fibonacci wrote about these numbers around 1200 CE. About how many years apart did they live?
activities.explanation: For years BCE and CE, add the numbers of years: a+b years. For example, a = 300 and b = 1202 gives 300+1202 = 1502 years.

activities.prompt: Put these events in time order, from earliest to latest.
items: Virahāṅka gave his method around 700 CE
Fibonacci wrote about the numbers in 1202 CE
activities.explanation: The dates run from 300 BCE to 700 CE to 1202 CE.

activities.prompt: A rhythm has 5 beats. Which group fills it exactly?
activities.explanation: One short beat plus two long beats gives 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 beats.
derived: one short and two long = 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 beats

activities.prompt: Virahāṅka gave his counting method around 702 CE, and Fibonacci wrote about these numbers around 1202 CE. About how many years later did Fibonacci write?
activities.explanation: Subtract the earlier year from the later year: b-a years. For example, a = 700 and b = 1202 gives 1202-700 = 502 years.

lessons.title: Digits in Disguise

activities.prompt: Can you uncover the hidden digits behind a letter puzzle?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Letters Can Hide Digits
activities.body: A cryptarithm replaces digits with letters. Each letter stands for one particular digit from 0 to 9. Cryptarithms are also called alphametics. When a one-digit number is added to itself twice, the sum can have two digits. Its units digit matches the original digit. A number like K2 can become HMM when added to itself.
keyPoints: Letters replace digits.
Each letter has one digit.
Cryptarithms are also called alphametics.
activities.explanation: Letters act as disguises for particular digits.

activities.title: Reading Cryptarithm Examples
activities.body: When a one-digit number is added to itself twice, the sum can have two digits. The units digit of the sum matches the original digit. In the first example, T is 5 and UT is 15. Another cryptarithm adds K2 to itself to make HMM. In the final cryptarithm, U is 9, T is 1 and A is 0.
keyPoints: The units digit stays the same.
Different examples use different letters.
Each letter represents one digit.
activities.explanation: These examples show how letters can hide digits in sums.

activities.prompt: What does a cryptarithm do?
activities.explanation: A cryptarithm replaces digits with letters.

activities.prompt: Each letter can represent a different digit every time it appears.
activities.explanation: Each letter represents one particular digit from 0 to 9.

activities.prompt: Match each cryptarithm part to its value.
activities.explanation: The lesson gives T as 5, UT as 15, U as 9 and A as 0.

activities.prompt: In the final cryptarithm, U is 9, T is 1 and A is 0. If a box has 5 copies of these 3 groups of marbles, how many marbles are in the box?
activities.explanation: U + T + A = 9 + 1 + 0 = 10 marbles in each copy. For 5 copies, n*(9+1+0) = 50 marbles.

activities.prompt: In a cryptarithm, T stands for 5. If a child has 5 marbles and receives 5 more groups of 5 marbles, how many marbles does the child have?
activities.explanation: There are 1+5 groups of 5 marbles, so 5*(1+5) = 30 marbles. When 5 is 2, the total is 15, and its units digit is 5 like T.

activities.prompt: A bulb starts on and is switched 79 times. After putting the switches into pairs, how many switches are left over?
activities.explanation: All the chosen switch counts are odd. The two halves differ by 1, so (s+1)/2-(s-1)/2 = 1 switch is left over and the bulb is off.

activities.prompt: The number after 2584 is 4181. A child writes 4181 on each of 3 cards. What is the sum of all the digits written on the cards?
activities.explanation: The next Virahanka number is 4181, and its digits add to 4+1+8+1 = 14. For 3 cards, n*(4+1+8+1) = 42.

activities.prompt: The 20th Virahanka term is even. For the term 987, how many terms are left over after making pairs?
activities.explanation: For an even term, the two halves are equal and the remainder is 0. For an odd term, they differ by 1. Thus (v+1)/2-(v-1)/2 = 1 term is left over.

activities.prompt: Put these Virahāṅka numbers in increasing order.
activities.explanation: The numbers increase from 987 to 1597 to 2584 to 4181.

activities.prompt: K stands for 3. Two price tags show K2 rupees. What is the total price in rupees?
activities.explanation: K2 means 10*k+2 rupees. Adding the two tags gives 2*(10*k+2) = 64 rupees. For k = 7, 72+72 = 144, which has the HMM form.

lessons.title: Triangle Basics and Equilateral Triangles

activities.prompt: What makes a triangle with perfectly matching sides so special?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet the Parts of a Triangle
activities.body: A triangle is the most basic closed shape in the chapter. It has three corner points, called vertices. Its sides join pairs of vertices. The sides at the corners form three angles. In triangle ABC, the angles are CAB, ABC and BCA. You may also call them A, B and C. An equilateral triangle is the most symmetric triangle. It has three equal sides.
keyPoints: A triangle has three vertices.
Its sides join pairs of vertices.
It has three angles.
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
activities.explanation: These are the main parts and names you need.

activities.prompt: A triangle has three corner points called vertices.
activities.explanation: Yes. A triangle has three corner points, called vertices.

activities.prompt: The sides of a triangle join pairs of ______.
activities.hint: These are the triangle's corner points.
activities.explanation: The sides join pairs of vertices.

activities.prompt: Match each triangle part with its name.
activities.explanation: Each pair matches a triangle part with its name.

activities.prompt: A row has 3 paper triangles. How many vertices are there on all 3 triangles altogether?
activities.explanation: Each triangle has 3 vertices, so the total number of vertices is 3 * 3 = 9 vertices.

activities.prompt: A box has 4 toy triangles. How many sides are there on all 4 triangles altogether?
activities.explanation: Each triangle has 3 sides, so the total number of sides is 4 * 3 = 12 sides.

activities.prompt: A bus has 3 triangle signs. How many angles are there on all 3 signs altogether?
activities.explanation: Each triangle has 3 angles, so the total number of angles is 3 * 3 = 9 angles.

activities.prompt: For 5 triangles like ABC, how many named angles are there in total?
activities.explanation: The angles of triangle ABC are CAB, ABC and BCA. Thus, 5 triangles have 5 * 3 = 15 named angles.

activities.prompt: In triangle ABC, the angles CAB, ABC and BCA may be called A, B and C. For 5 such triangles, how many one-letter angle names are there?
activities.explanation: Each triangle has the three one-letter angle names A, B and C, so the total is 5 * 3 = 15 angle names.

activities.prompt: Put the full angle names in your book's order.
activities.explanation: Your book lists the full angle names in this order.

activities.prompt: Meera writes the vertices of 4 triangles in any order. How many vertices are written altogether?
activities.explanation: Changing the order does not change the 3 vertices of each triangle, so the total is 4 * 3 = 12 vertices.

lessons.title: Constructing a Triangle from Three Sides

activities.prompt: Can you turn three side lengths into a triangle?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Constructing the triangle
activities.body: You can construct a triangle from given sides using only a marked ruler. First, take AC as 5 cm and BC as 6 cm. Construct the base AB with one side length. Draw a circle centred at A and reaching 5 cm from A. Then construct an arc reaching 6 cm from B. The arcs meet at C, the third vertex. Finally, join AC and BC to complete the triangle.
keyPoints: A marked ruler is enough.
AC is 5 cm and BC is 6 cm.
The arcs meet at C, the third vertex.
activities.explanation: This shows how the arcs fix the third vertex.

activities.title: Choosing the tool
activities.prompt: Which statement about the construction is true?
options: Point C comes before the arcs.
The base can have any length.
activities.explanation: Correct! A marked ruler is enough for this construction.

activities.title: Constructing the base
activities.prompt: The base AB is constructed with one of the side lengths.
activities.explanation: Yes. The base AB uses one of the given side lengths.

activities.title: Matching the construction details
activities.prompt: Match each construction detail with its correct detail.
activities.explanation: Well done. The arcs use centres A and B.

activities.title: Putting the construction in order
activities.prompt: Put the construction steps in the correct order.
items: Construct base AB with one side length.
Draw the circle centred at A, reaching 5 cm.
Construct an arc reaching 6 cm from B.
Mark C where the arcs meet.
activities.explanation: Correct order. The arcs locate C before the sides are joined.

activities.prompt: Start the marked-ruler construction by taking 7 cm as the base AB of the triangle. How long is AB in cm?
activities.explanation: AB is one chosen side of the triangle. For example, if 7 = 5, then AB = 5 cm.

activities.prompt: Draw a circle with centre A and radius 4 cm. How long is AC in cm?
activities.explanation: C lies on the circle centred at A, so AC is the radius. For example, if 4 = 4, then AC = 4 cm.

activities.prompt: Construct an arc of radius 6 cm from B. How long is BC in cm?
activities.explanation: C lies on the arc drawn from B, so BC is the radius of that arc. For example, if 6 = 6, then BC = 6 cm.

activities.prompt: The two arcs meet at C. If AC is 3 cm and BC is 6 cm, how many cm longer is BC than AC?
activities.explanation: Subtract the shorter radius from the longer radius. For example, 6 - 3 = 3 cm.

activities.prompt: Join AC and BC to complete the triangle. If AC is 5 cm and BC is 7 cm, what is their total length in cm?
activities.explanation: Add the lengths of the two joined sides. For example, 4 + 6 = 10 cm.

activities.prompt: A constructed triangle has AB = 7 cm, AC = 5 cm, and BC = 8 cm. What is the total length of its three sides in cm?
activities.explanation: Add all three side lengths. For example, 5 + 4 + 6 = 15 cm.

lessons.title: Checking Three Side Lengths

activities.prompt: Can three lengths always make a triangle?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Triangle Inequality
activities.body: The direct straight-line path is shorter than a path through a third point. For triangle lengths, compare each length with the sum of the other two lengths. This condition is called the triangle inequality. A triangle exists whenever the lengths satisfy it. The set 3, 4, 5 satisfies it. The set 10, 15, 30 does not.
keyPoints: Compare each length with the sum of the others.
The rule is called the triangle inequality.
A triangle exists when the given lengths satisfy the rule.
activities.explanation: Compare every length before deciding whether a triangle exists.

activities.title: Comparing Circles
activities.body: The circles touch when the two smaller lengths add to the longest length. If their sum is less than the longest length, the circles do not intersect. Here, intersect means the circles cross. If their sum is more than the longest length, the circles intersect. Compare the sum with the longest length.
keyPoints: When the sum equals the longest length, the circles touch.
When the sum is less, the circles do not intersect.
When the sum is more, the circles intersect.
activities.explanation: The sum of the smaller lengths decides the circle outcome.

activities.prompt: The set 3, 4, 5 satisfies the triangle inequality.
activities.explanation: Each length in this set is smaller than the sum of the others.

activities.prompt: Match each set or rule with its correct description.
pairs: Each length is smaller than the sum of the others
Does not satisfy the triangle inequality
activities.explanation: Only the set 3, 4, 5 satisfies the rule. The set 10, 15, 30 does not.

activities.prompt: Put the comparisons in order from the smallest sum to the largest sum.
items: The sum is less than the longest length
The sum equals the longest length
The sum is more than the longest length
activities.explanation: The order runs from less than to equal to more than.

activities.prompt: A bus goes directly 4 km to school. The route through the market is 9 km. How many km longer is the route through the market?
activities.explanation: For d = 4 km and p = 8 km, p - d = 8 - 4 = 4 km.

activities.prompt: Three sticks are 12 cm, 17 cm and 30 cm long, and 30 cm is the longest. How many cm longer is the longest stick than the sum of the other two sticks?
activities.explanation: For a = 10, b = 15 and c = 30, c - a - b = 30 - 10 - 15 = 5 cm. A length of 30 cm cannot be used with 10 cm and 15 cm.

activities.prompt: The set 10, 15, 30 can form a triangle.
activities.explanation: The lengths 10 cm, 15 cm and 30 cm cannot form a triangle. They fail the triangle inequality.

activities.prompt: Two smaller circles have lengths 5 cm each, and the largest circle has length 6 cm, which is twice 5 cm. By how many cm does the sum of the two smaller lengths differ from the longest length?
activities.explanation: For a = 3 and c = 6, a + a - c = 3 + 3 - 6 = 0 cm. The circles just touch.

activities.prompt: Two smaller circles have lengths 3 cm and 3 cm, and the largest circle has length 10 cm. How many cm shorter is the sum of the two smaller lengths than the longest length?
activities.explanation: For a = 2, b = 3 and c = 8, c - a - b = 8 - 2 - 3 = 3 cm. The circles do not intersect.

activities.prompt: Have you ever built a triangle from just its sides and angles?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How to Construct a Triangle
activities.body: Constructing a triangle needs clear drawing steps. For example, draw AB as 5 cm. Draw angle A as 45°. Mark point C on the other arm. Join BC to finish the triangle. If two angles are given, the side touching both is the included side. Their sum must be less than 180° for a triangle to exist. The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°.
keyPoints: Draw the side and given angle.
Mark C, then join BC.
The included side touches both given angles.
Two given angles must sum to less than 180°.
activities.explanation: These steps help you construct a triangle from given sides and angles.

activities.title: Start the Construction
activities.prompt: After drawing AB as 5 cm, what should you do next?
options: Join BC to finish the triangle.
activities.explanation: Construct angle A by drawing its other arm. Mark C on that arm.

activities.title: Two Given Angles
activities.prompt: Two given angles add to less than 180°. What can you construct?
activities.explanation: A triangle exists whenever two given angles add to less than 180°.

activities.title: Finish the First Triangle
activities.prompt: Put these construction steps in the correct order.

Join BC to finish the triangle.
activities.explanation: The angle comes before point C. Joining BC then completes the required triangle.

activities.title: Check the Angle Total

activities.explanation: Every triangle has three angles. These angles add up to 180°.

activities.prompt: A triangular kite has AB 7 cm, AC 8 cm, and angle A between them. What is the length in cm of the included side AB?
activities.explanation: The included side is AB, so its length is 7 cm.

activities.prompt: Point C is marked on the other arm of angle A so that AC is 4 cm. How many cm from A is point C?
activities.explanation: Point C is marked 4 cm from A on the other arm.

activities.prompt: Angle A is 45°, and its other arm is drawn. What is the size in degrees of angle A?
activities.explanation: The angle between AB and the other arm is 45°.

activities.prompt: AB is 6 cm, AC is 5 cm, and the new side BC is 7 cm. What is the total length in cm of the three joined sides?
activities.explanation: The three joined sides are AB, AC, and BC. Their total length is 6 + 5 + 7 cm.

activities.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle A is 45°, angle B is 80°, and AB is 5 cm. What is the length in cm of the included side AB?
activities.explanation: AB belongs to both given angles, so AB is the included side. Its length is 5 cm.

activities.prompt: The arms of angle A and angle B meet at point C. Angle A is 30° and angle B is 40°. What is the size in degrees of angle C?
activities.explanation: The three angles add to 180°, so angle C = 180 - (30 + 40) = 110°.

lessons.title: Exterior Angles and Altitudes

activities.prompt: Can you find the secret angles and heights hiding in a triangle?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Exterior Angles and Altitudes
activities.body: An exterior angle forms when one side is extended and joined to another side. An altitude is a segment drawn perpendicular from a vertex. Perpendicular means crossing at a right angle. Here, AD is perpendicular to BC, so AD is an altitude. The other altitudes are perpendiculars from the other vertices. Height depends on the chosen base.
keyPoints: An exterior angle uses an extended side.
An altitude is drawn perpendicular to a side.
The height depends on the chosen base.
activities.explanation: Altitudes help us measure a triangle's height from different bases.

activities.title: Find the Exterior Angle
activities.prompt: Which choice describes an exterior angle?
options: Between an extended side and another side
Between a vertex and its opposite side
Between a base and its height
activities.explanation: An exterior angle forms when a side is extended and joined to another side.

activities.prompt: Segment AD is one of the triangle's altitudes.
activities.explanation: AD is drawn perpendicular to BC, so it is an altitude.

activities.title: Match the Ideas
activities.prompt: Match each statement with its matching idea.
activities.explanation: Each altitude is perpendicular, and the height changes with the chosen base.

activities.prompt: Side CA of a playground triangle is extended. The exterior angle ACD measures 140°. What is the measure of exterior angle ACD in degrees?
activities.explanation: An exterior angle is formed between an extended side and another side. Angle ACD measures 140°, so the answer is 140°.

activities.prompt: Exterior angle ACD measures 120°. How many degrees larger is it than a right angle?
activities.explanation: A right angle measures 90°. The difference is 120 - 90 = 30°.

activities.prompt: In triangle ABC, AD is perpendicular to BC and AD is 4 cm long. DE is 8 cm and EF is 9 cm. What is the length of the altitude from A in cm?
activities.explanation: AD is the altitude from A because it is perpendicular to BC. Its length is 4 cm.

activities.prompt: The three altitudes of a toy triangle measure 10 cm, 5 cm and 12 cm. What is their total length in cm?
activities.explanation: The total length of the three altitudes is 10 + 5 + 12 = 27 cm.

activities.title: Meet the Triangle Types
activities.body: Triangles can be grouped by their sides or their angles. By sides, equilateral triangles have equal sides. Isosceles triangles have two equal sides. Scalene triangles have three different side lengths. By angles, a right-angled triangle has one right angle. An obtuse-angled triangle has one obtuse angle. An acute-angled triangle has three acute angles.
keyPoints: Equilateral triangles have equal sides.
Isosceles triangles have two equal sides.
Scalene triangles have three different side lengths.
Angle types include right-angled, obtuse-angled and acute-angled.
activities.explanation: These groups help you describe triangles clearly.

activities.prompt: An equilateral triangular sign has sides 5 cm, 5 cm, and 5 cm. What is the length of each side in cm?

activities.prompt: A display has 2 right-angled triangular cards. How many right angles are there in all the cards?

activities.prompt: A shop has 5 triangular signs with one obtuse angle each. How many obtuse angles are there altogether?

activities.prompt: An acute-angled triangle has one obtuse angle.

activities.prompt: An equilateral triangular mat has sides 5 cm each. What is the combined length of its three sides in cm?
activities.explanation: There are three equal sides, so their combined length is 3*s cm.

lessons.title: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number

activities.prompt: Ready to discover what happens when a fraction meets a whole number?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A fraction multiplication method
activities.body: Multiplying a fraction uses the same method as multiplying by a whole number. For two-fifths, the denominator is 5 and the numerator is 2. Divide the fraction by its denominator. Then, multiply by its numerator. Multiplying two-fifths by 3 gives six-fifths. You can use this method in distance and time problems.
keyPoints: Multiply a fraction like you multiply a whole number.
Divide by the denominator first.
Then multiply by the numerator.
activities.explanation: Start with the fraction, then follow the two steps.

activities.explanation: A fraction counts equal parts of a whole.

activities.prompt: A child fills 2 bags, each to three-fourths of a capacity of 4 marbles. How many marbles are in all the bags?

activities.prompt: A tortoise walks three-fourths of a kilometre in each of 4 equal hours. What total distance does it walk in kilometres?
activities.explanation: Total distance = number of hours × distance in each hour = 4 × 3/4 = 3 kilometres.

activities.prompt: A bus waits for three-fourths of an hour during each of 4 trips. What is the total waiting time in hours?
activities.explanation: Total waiting time = number of trips × waiting time per trip = 4 × 3/4 = 3 hours.

activities.explanation: A session lasts 5/4 hours, so 10/4 hour is n/5 of a session. The cost is 10*(n/5) rupees.

activities.title: Multiplying fractions
activities.body: Use a unit square to show each fraction of a whole. One-half of one-fourth makes one-eighth. The tortoise walks three-tenths of a kilometre in three-fourths of an hour. This happens at two-fifths of a kilometre per hour. Another example is three-fourths multiplied by two-fifths, which gives three-tenths.
keyPoints: A unit square shows a fraction of a whole.
One-half times one-fourth equals one-eighth.
Three-fourths times two-fifths equals three-tenths.
The tortoise walks three-tenths of a kilometre in three-fourths of an hour.
activities.explanation: Fractions can be shown with equal parts and multiplied using matching fractions.

activities.prompt: A grid with 5 rows and 4 columns has 20 equal parts.

activities.prompt: What does a unit square help us show?

activities.prompt: The tortoise walks ______ of a kilometre in half an hour.
activities.hint: Look at the distance covered during that time.

activities.prompt: A unit square is divided into 2 equal parts, and 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the square is shaded?
activities.explanation: One shaded part out of 2 equal parts is the fraction 1/2.

activities.prompt: One-fourth of a bus route is split into 4 equal parts. What fraction of the whole route is one part?
activities.explanation: Dividing one-fourth into 4 equal parts gives 1/(4 × 4) of the whole route.

activities.prompt: A child has 16 rupees. She spends one-half of one-fourth of the money. How many rupees does she spend?
activities.explanation: One-half of one-fourth is one-eighth, so the child spends 16/8 rupees.

activities.prompt: A tile grid has 3 rows and 6 columns of equal squares. How many equal parts does the grid have?
activities.explanation: The number of equal parts is the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.

activities.prompt: A path is shown by a grid with 5 rows and 4 columns, making 20 equal parts. The tortoise covers 2 parts, and each part is 1/20 of a kilometre. How far does it walk in kilometres?
activities.explanation: The distance is 2 parts multiplied by 1/20 kilometre for each part.

activities.prompt: Multiplying three-fourths by two-fifths gives two-fifths.
activities.explanation: Multiplying three-fourths by two-fifths gives three-tenths. You checked the product carefully.

activities.prompt: A vendor has 2/10 kilograms of laddoos. A buyer buys 9/4 of the laddoos. How many kilograms does the buyer get?
activities.explanation: Three-fourths of two-fifths is three-tenths, so the buyer gets 3/10 kilogram.

lessons.title: Comparing products and changing the order

activities.title: How products change
activities.body: Multiplying a number by 1 leaves the product unchanged. When both numbers are greater than 1, their product is greater than both. If one number is between 0 and 1, the product is less than the other number. Changing the order of multiplication does not matter. A rectangle also keeps its area when its length and breadth are interchanged.
keyPoints: Multiplying by 1 leaves the product unchanged.
The order of multiplication does not matter.
Interchanging length and breadth keeps a rectangle's area.
activities.explanation: These rules help you compare products and check them easily.

lessons.title: Dividing fractions

activities.prompt: How can dividing fractions feel as easy as flipping a pancake?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How to divide fractions
activities.body: Divide fractions by changing the divisor into its reciprocal, then multiply. The reciprocal is made by reversing the numerator and denominator. For example, three-thirds divided by two-thirds equals nine-halves. One-fifth divided by one-half equals two-fifths. Two-thirds divided by three-fifths equals ten-ninths. When the divisor is between 0 and 1, the quotient is greater than the dividend.
keyPoints: Division can be restated as a multiplication problem.
Find the divisor’s reciprocal.
Multiply the dividend by that reciprocal.
activities.explanation: Reciprocals turn fraction division into multiplication.

activities.title: Find the first step

options: Add the divisor to the dividend
activities.explanation: The first step is to find the reciprocal of the divisor.

activities.prompt: A pot has 4 kg of laddoos. Which multiplication gives the kg of laddoos each child gets when the pot is divided equally between 2 children?
activities.explanation: Dividing by 2 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 1/2. Thus n*(1/2) gives the kg for each child.

activities.prompt: Which fraction is the reciprocal of 2/4?
activities.explanation: Reversing the numerator and denominator of n/4 gives 4/n.

activities.prompt: Before dividing by 1/5, which number should be used as the reciprocal?

activities.title: Put the steps in order
activities.prompt: Put these ideas in the lesson’s order.

activities.explanation: Division can become multiplication by using the divisor’s reciprocal.

activities.prompt: A worker has 8/5 kg of rice and shares it equally among 8/2 people. How many kg of rice does each person get?
activities.explanation: Divide the dividend n/5 by the divisor n/2: (n/5)/(n/2) = 2/5 kg.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Re-creating and Checking the Symbol

activities.prompt: How can we make a symbol match perfectly, even after turning it over?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Re-creating and Checking a Symbol
activities.body: Tracing is difficult when a symbol is big. Two arm lengths do not determine it exactly. We also need the angle between them, the gap between the arms. Three suitable measurements can make an exact replica. Congruent figures have the same shape and size. They fit perfectly when placed one over another. Non-congruent figures do not. We may rotate or flip a figure before checking.
keyPoints: Big symbols are difficult to trace.
The angle and arm lengths are needed.
Congruent figures fit exactly one over another.
activities.explanation: Measure carefully, then check the fit by tracing.

activities.title: When Is Tracing Difficult?
activities.prompt: According to the lesson, when is tracing difficult?

activities.title: Tracing as a Check
activities.prompt: Tracing one figure can help us check whether it fits another figure.
activities.explanation: Tracing shows whether one figure fits another exactly.

activities.title: Match Each Idea

activities.prompt: A bus decoration has two symbol arms, 5 cm and 4 cm long. How many cm of paper are needed to trace both arms?

activities.prompt: Two symbols have the same arm lengths. Their angles are 45° and 75°. What is the difference between their angles in degrees?
activities.explanation: The difference between the angles is 75 - 45 = 30°. Different angles can make the symbols non-congruent.

activities.prompt: Two symbols have the same arms, 5 cm and 6 cm. Their angles are 30° and 60°. How many degrees must be added to the second angle to make it equal the first?
activities.explanation: The needed angle change is 60 - 30 = 30°. Together with the two arm lengths, this gives the same three measurements.

activities.prompt: A paper symbol has arms 9 cm and 8 cm. A second symbol is congruent to it. How many cm long are the two arms of the second symbol together?
activities.explanation: Congruent symbols have the same shape and size, so the second symbol has arms of 9 cm and 8 cm. Their total length is 17 cm.

activities.prompt: How can three side lengths reveal whether two triangles match perfectly?

activities.title: Triangle Side Lengths and Congruence
activities.body: Triangles are congruent when they have the same three side lengths. This rule is called SSS, which means Side Side Side. The girls measure 40 cm, 60 cm, and 80 cm. These lengths can produce a triangle congruent to the original. Angles are not needed when all three side lengths are known. In a congruence statement, each vertex must match its corresponding vertex.
keyPoints: Congruent triangles have the same three side lengths.
SSS means Side Side Side.
Angles are not needed when all three sides are known.
activities.explanation: Great! Knowing all three sides lets you check congruence using SSS.

activities.prompt: The girls measured sides of 40 cm, 60 cm, and ______ cm.
activities.hint: Think of the three measured side lengths.
activities.explanation: The three side lengths are 40 cm, 60 cm, and 80 cm.

activities.prompt: Triangles with the same three side lengths are congruent.
activities.explanation: Yes! Matching all three side lengths gives congruent triangles.

activities.prompt: What does SSS mean?
activities.explanation: SSS means Side Side Side. It uses all three side lengths.

activities.prompt: A triangle has side lengths 30 cm, 50 cm, and 80 cm. What is the total length of the three measured sides in cm?
activities.explanation: Total side length = 30 + 50 + 80 = 160 cm.

activities.prompt: Rabia uses radii of 4 cm and 8 cm to draw two circles. What is the sum of the two radii in cm?
activities.explanation: Sum of the radii = 4 + 8 = 12 cm.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to show congruence.
items: Check that all three lengths match
activities.explanation: Measure the sides first. Then check them, use SSS, and match the vertices.

activities.prompt: Triangle ABE has AB = 10 cm, AE = 10 cm, and BE = 9 cm. Triangles ABE and ABF are congruent. What is the length of BF in cm?
activities.explanation: BE corresponds to BF, so BF = 9 cm.

activities.prompt: Triangle ABC has AB = 12 cm, BC = 11 cm, and CA = 10 cm. Vertex A corresponds to X, B to Y, and C to Z. What is the length of XY in cm?
activities.explanation: A corresponds to X and B corresponds to Y, so XY matches AB. Therefore, XY = 12 cm.

activities.prompt: Triangle ACB has AC = 8 cm, CB = 11 cm, and BA = 8 cm. In the correct statement ACB ≅ XZY, what is the length of ZY in cm?
activities.explanation: C corresponds to Z and B corresponds to Y, so ZY matches CB. Therefore, ZY = 11 cm.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Angles, SAS and SSA

activities.prompt: Can two sides and an angle sometimes make two different triangles?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Angles, SAS and SSA
activities.body: Using 30°, 70°, and 80° draws many triangles. These triangles can have different sizes. Two sides and their included angle can determine a triangle. The included angle is the angle between those sides. This is SAS, meaning Side Angle Side. Two sides with a non-included angle form SSA. SSA may give two triangles that do not match exactly. Both possible triangles can satisfy the measurements.
keyPoints: 30°, 70°, and 80° do not fix triangle size.
SAS means Side Angle Side.
SSA may give two possible triangles.
activities.explanation: You now know how SAS and SSA use sides and angles.

activities.prompt: What happens when 30°, 70°, and 80° are used?
activities.explanation: These angles do not fix a triangle's size. Many different triangles can be drawn.

activities.prompt: The angles 30°, 70°, and 80° fix the size of a triangle.
activities.explanation: These angles do not fix the triangle's size. Different-sized triangles can be drawn.

activities.prompt: SAS means Side ______ Side.
activities.hint: This part sits between the two sides.
activities.explanation: SAS means Side Angle Side. It uses two sides and their included angle.

activities.prompt: Match each condition or result to its clue.
pairs: Uses two sides and their included angle
Uses two sides and a non-included angle
activities.explanation: SAS uses an included angle. SSA uses a non-included angle and may give two non-congruent triangles.

activities.prompt: Triangle A has angles 30°, 70°, and 80° and a perimeter of 20 cm. Triangle B has the same angles, with every side 4 times as long. What is Triangle B's perimeter in cm?
activities.explanation: The same angles can make triangles of different sizes. Multiplying every side by 4 multiplies the perimeter by 4, so the new perimeter is 20*4 cm.

activities.prompt: A child draws 4 triangles with angles 30°, 70°, and 80°, using a different side length for each triangle. How many non-congruent triangles are drawn?
activities.explanation: Triangles with the same angles can have different sizes. Since all 4 sizes are different, the number of non-congruent triangles is 4.

activities.prompt: A triangular bus sign has sides 5 cm and 4 cm, with a fixed angle between them. How many different triangles can these measurements make?
activities.explanation: Two sides and their included angle determine one triangle. Thus the correct formula gives 1 triangle.

activities.prompt: A triangular flag has side 3 cm, included angle 60°, and side 8 cm. Its third side is 5 cm. What is the flag's perimeter in cm?
activities.explanation: The data are in the order Side-Angle-Side, so they give the SAS condition. The perimeter is 3+8+5 cm.

activities.prompt: A triangular road sign has sides 3 cm and 4 cm and angle 50°, but the angle is not between the two sides. How many measurements are given?
activities.explanation: There are two side measurements and one angle measurement. This Side-Side-Angle situation is called the SSA condition.

activities.prompt: Two sides and a non-included angle in an SSA problem give two possible triangles. How many of these triangles satisfy all the given measurements?
activities.explanation: Both possible triangles satisfy the two given sides and the given non-included angle. Therefore, the correct formula gives 2 triangles.

activities.prompt: How can we prove two triangles are identical using angles and sides?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Triangle congruence conditions
activities.body: Triangles can be shown to be congruent when two angles and their included side are known. This is the ASA condition, meaning Angle Side Angle. The AAS condition also guarantees congruence. The RHS condition guarantees congruence too. The side opposite the right angle is called the hypotenuse. In the lesson, triangles AOB and DOC are congruent because they satisfy the SAS condition.
keyPoints: Two angles and the included side prove congruence.
ASA means Angle Side Angle.
AAS and RHS guarantee congruence.
activities.explanation: These conditions help you recognise congruent triangles.

activities.title: The AAS condition
activities.prompt: Which statement about AAS is correct?
options: The AAS condition is the name of the hypotenuse.
The AAS condition names vertically opposite angles.
The AAS condition means Angle Side Angle.
activities.explanation: The lesson states that the AAS condition guarantees congruence.

activities.prompt: The RHS condition guarantees congruence.
activities.explanation: Yes, the lesson states that the RHS condition guarantees congruence.

activities.title: Name the hypotenuse
activities.prompt: The side opposite the right angle is called the ______.
activities.hint: This special side lies opposite the right angle.
activities.explanation: This side is opposite the right angle.

activities.title: Match each clue with its result

activities.prompt: A triangular bus-stop sign has angles 40° and 30°. What is the third angle in degrees?
activities.explanation: The angles of a triangle add to 180°, so the third angle is 180 - (40 + 30) = 110°.

activities.prompt: Two triangular bus signs are congruent by ASA. The included side of each sign is 10 cm. What is the length of the included side in cm?
activities.explanation: ASA means Angle Side Angle. Congruent triangles have equal matching sides, so the included side is 10 cm.

activities.prompt: Point O is the midpoint of road segment AD. If AD is 12 cm long, what is the length of OD in cm?
activities.explanation: O is the midpoint, so AO = OD. Therefore, OD = 12/2 = 6 cm.

activities.prompt: Two roads cross at O. Angle AOB is 60°. What is the measure of vertically opposite angle DOC in degrees?
activities.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so angle DOC is 60°.

activities.prompt: A right triangular road sign has two sides 6 cm and 8 cm. The side opposite the right angle is 5 cm. What is the hypotenuse length in cm?
activities.explanation: The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse, so its length is 5 cm.

activities.prompt: Two triangular kite designs are congruent by AAS. The matching side that is not between the two given angles is 5 cm in each. What is its length in cm?
activities.explanation: AAS guarantees congruence. Congruent triangles have equal matching sides, so the side is 5 cm.

activities.prompt: What makes an isosceles triangle special, and can you prove it?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Equal Sides and Equal Angles
activities.body: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides. Triangle ABC has AB = AC. An altitude is drawn from A to BC. It makes two right angles at D. Triangles ADB and ADC share AD. They have equal sides AB and AC. So they satisfy the RHS condition. Therefore, angles B and C are equal. An equilateral triangle has three equal sides. Its angles are equal, and each is 60°.
keyPoints: Triangle ABC is isosceles because AB = AC.
The altitude creates two right angles at D.
An equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
activities.explanation: The altitude and RHS condition show that angles B and C are equal.

activities.title: The Altitude
activities.prompt: The altitude creates two right angles at D.
activities.explanation: Yes. The altitude from A creates two right angles at D.

activities.title: Match Side and Angle Facts
activities.prompt: Match each side fact to its angle fact, or its angle sum.
activities.explanation: Equal sides lead to equal opposite angles. The three equal angles total 180°.

activities.title: Angles of an Equilateral Triangle
activities.body: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal. A triangle's equal sides have equal angles opposite them. So all three angles are equal. The three angles add up to 180°. Dividing 180° by 3 gives 60°. Therefore, each angle is 60°. Equal sides help us find equal angles.
keyPoints: Equal sides have equal angles opposite them.
The three equal angles add up to 180°.
Each angle is 60°.
activities.explanation: The equal sides make all three angles equal. Each angle measures 60°.

activities.title: Use the Equal-Sides Rule
activities.prompt: Which equal sides give equal angles A and C?
activities.explanation: Equal sides AB and BC give equal angles A and C.

activities.title: Check the Angles
activities.prompt: In an equilateral triangle, only two angles are equal.
activities.explanation: All three angles are equal in an equilateral triangle. Each angle is 60°.

activities.prompt: An altitude AD of 3 cm meets BC at D in triangle ABC. What is the size of angle ADB in degrees?
activities.explanation: An altitude creates two right angles at D. Formula: 90 degrees.

activities.prompt: Triangle ABC has AB = AC = 6 cm and altitude AD = 5 cm. How many triangles are compared in the RHS condition?
activities.explanation: Triangles ADB and ADC satisfy the RHS condition. Formula: 1+1 = 2 triangles.

activities.prompt: An equilateral triangular laddoo packet has three sides of 9 cm each. What is the size of each angle in degrees?
activities.explanation: The three equal angles add to 180 degrees. Formula: 180/3 = 60 degrees.

activities.title: Congruence in Real Life
activities.body: Congruent figures have the same shape and size. You may rotate or flip one to fit another. Congruent triangles appear in many constructions and designs. The SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS conditions guarantee congruence. Congruence can hold when the given side is not between the angles. An equilateral triangle has every angle equal to 60°.
keyPoints: Congruent figures have the same shape and size.
Rotation and flipping may help figures fit.
SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS guarantee congruence.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you recognise and check congruent figures.

activities.title: Same Shape and Size
activities.prompt: Figures with the same shape and size are congruent.
activities.explanation: Congruent figures have the same shape and size.

activities.title: Find the Congruent Pair
activities.prompt: Which pair shows congruent triangles?
activities.explanation: Congruent triangles have the same shape and size.

activities.title: Match the Ideas

pairs: have the same shape and size
Every angle of an equilateral triangle
activities.explanation: Rotation and flipping help figures fit. Congruent figures have the same shape and size.

activities.prompt: A laddoo-box design has 3 rows with 3 identical triangular tiles in each row. How many congruent triangular tiles are in the design?

activities.prompt: A square bus sign is 2 cm on each side. It is rotated and then flipped. What is the total length of its 4 sides in cm?

activities.prompt: Two triangular bus signs have the same side lengths 4 cm, 2 cm, and 3 cm. What is the perimeter of one sign in cm?
activities.explanation: The signs are congruent by SSS because all three sides match. Perimeter = 4 + 2 + 3 = 3 + 4 + 5 = 9 cm.

activities.prompt: Two triangular braces have matching sides 4 cm and 3 cm and a matching included angle of 90°. What is the sum of the two matching side lengths in cm?
activities.explanation: Matching sides and their included angle guarantee congruence by SAS. Sum of the sides = 4 + 3 = 3 + 5 = 8 cm.

activities.prompt: Two triangles have matching angles 20° and 20°. Their matching side 3 cm is not between the two angles. What is the sum of the matching angle measures in degrees?
activities.explanation: The triangles are congruent by ASA even though the matching side is not between the angles. Sum of angles = 20 + 20 = 40 + 50 = 40°.

activities.title: Reason About Opposite Angles
activities.prompt: Put the angle reasoning steps in order.
items: Conclude that these angles are equal.
activities.explanation: Angles opposite equal sides in a triangle are equal.

activities.prompt: Two right-triangle tiles match by RHS. Their side lengths are 3*1 cm, 4*1 cm, and 5*1 cm. What is the perimeter of one tile in cm?
activities.explanation: The matching right angle, sides, and hypotenuse guarantee congruence by RHS. Perimeter = 3*1 + 4*1 + 5*1 = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm.

lessons.title: Integers, sums and differences

activities.prompt: Can you uncover Rakesh’s numbers and find his final place on a number line?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Moving with integers
activities.body: Rightward movement is positive, while leftward movement is negative. A number line is used to model movements in both directions. A signed movement gives both the distance and the direction of movement. After two rightward strikes, add the movements to find the final position. Trying pairs and checking sums and differences can reveal two numbers. For example, 5 units right followed by 7 units left ends at −2.
keyPoints: Rightward movement is positive.
Leftward movement is negative.
Add movements to find the final position.
activities.explanation: These rules help you solve puzzles and track movement.

activities.title: Jump along the number line

tasks.then: You cross zero and land on -4.
A number and its opposite make zero.

activities.takeaway: Adding a negative moves left, adding a positive moves right.
activities.explanation: Adding a negative moves left, adding a positive moves right.

activities.title: Finding a difference
activities.prompt: The difference is found by taking the first number minus the second number.
activities.explanation: Yes. Subtract the second number from the first to find the difference.

activities.title: A final position
activities.prompt: Moving 5 units right, then 7 units left gives a final position of what?
activities.explanation: 5 right is positive and 7 left is negative. Adding them gives −2.

activities.title: Match the puzzle clues
activities.prompt: Match each puzzle clue to its number.
activities.explanation: Each clue matches the number given for that part of Rakesh’s puzzles.

activities.title: Order the movement
activities.prompt: Put these movement steps in the order shown in the lesson.
items: Add the movements for the final position
activities.explanation: The movement goes right first, then left. The two movements are then added.

activities.prompt: Rakesh has two laddoo counts. Their sum is 35 and the first minus the second is 7. How many laddoos are in the first count?
activities.explanation: Add the sum and difference, then divide by 2. For example, (25 + 5) / 2 = 10 laddoos.

activities.prompt: Rakesh tries pairs of bus numbers. The pair must have sum 21 and first-minus-second difference 5. How many buses are in the second number?
activities.explanation: Subtract the difference from the sum, then divide by 2. For example, (21 - 3) / 2 = 9 buses.

activities.prompt: A toy bus starts at 2 cm on a number line. It moves 7 cm right and then 2 cm right. What is its final position in cm?
activities.explanation: Both movements are rightward, so add them to the starting position. For example, 2 + 5 + 4 = 11 cm.

activities.prompt: A marble moves 18 cm right and then 7 cm left. What is its signed movement in cm?
activities.explanation: Right is positive and left is negative. For example, 5 - 7 = -2 cm.

activities.prompt: A marble starts at 5 cm on a number line, moves 12 cm right, and then moves 10 cm left. What is its final position in cm?
activities.explanation: Add the rightward movement and subtract the leftward movement from the starting position. For example, 3 + 12 - 6 = 9 cm.

activities.prompt: A toy bus starts at 0 cm, moves 18 cm right, and then moves some cm left. It ends at 8 cm. How many cm was the leftward movement?
activities.explanation: The final position is the rightward movement minus the leftward movement. For example, 12 - 5 = 7 cm left.

lessons.title: Tokens, subtraction and additive inverses

activities.prompt: Can one red token help us subtract a much bigger number?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How tokens show subtraction
activities.body: A green token stands for positive 1, and a red token stands for negative 1. One green and one red token cancel, making zero. To subtract 18 from 7, add eleven zero pairs. This lets you remove 18 positive tokens. Eleven red tokens remain, so 7 − 18 equals −11. An additive inverse is the opposite number that makes a sum zero. Subtracting a number means adding its additive inverse.
keyPoints: Green tokens show positive 1, and red tokens show negative 1.
One green and one red token make zero.
Subtracting a number means adding its additive inverse.
activities.explanation: Tokens help us see why subtracting can leave negative tokens.

activities.prompt: What does a green token represent?
activities.explanation: A green token represents positive 1.

activities.prompt: A green token and a red token together make zero.
activities.explanation: The tokens cancel each other, so their total is zero.

activities.prompt: Match each token group to its value.
activities.explanation: The two tokens have opposite values and cancel each other.

activities.prompt: Put the steps for finding (+7) – (+18) in order.
activities.explanation: The zero pairs provide enough tokens to remove all 18 positives.

activities.title: Subtracting means adding the inverse
activities.body: An additive inverse is the opposite number that makes a sum zero. The additive inverse of 18 is −18. The additive inverse of −18 is 18. So subtracting a number means adding its additive inverse. For example, subtracting 18 is the same as adding −18.
keyPoints: An additive inverse is an opposite number.
The additive inverse of 18 is −18.
Subtracting means adding the additive inverse.
activities.explanation: Adding an inverse changes subtraction into addition.

activities.prompt: Which number should you add when you subtract 18 from 7?
activities.explanation: Subtracting 18 is the same as adding its additive inverse, −18.

activities.prompt: The additive inverse of −18 is ______.
activities.hint: Find the opposite number that makes the sum zero.
activities.explanation: The opposite of −18 is 18, so these numbers make zero together.

activities.prompt: Subtracting 18 is the same as adding −18.
activities.explanation: The additive inverse of 18 is −18, so subtraction means adding −18.

activities.prompt: A tray has 9 green tokens. What positive number do the green tokens represent?
activities.explanation: Each green token represents positive 1, so 9 green tokens represent 9 positive token units.

activities.prompt: A tray has 7 positive tokens. How many zero pairs must be added so that 20 positive tokens can be removed?
activities.explanation: Each zero pair adds one positive token and one negative token. Adding 20 - (7) zero pairs provides enough positive tokens to remove 20 positives.

lessons.title: Multiplying integers with tokens

activities.prompt: Can we use tokens to discover what happens when negative integers meet?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: How tokens show multiplication
activities.body: Tokens are counting objects in a bag. A positive multiplier adds tokens. A negative multiplier removes them. In 4 × 2, add 2 positive tokens 4 times. This gives 8 positive tokens. A negative multiplier can also remove positive tokens. Two negative multipliers remove negative tokens. Their product is positive.
keyPoints: A positive multiplier places tokens in the bag.
A negative multiplier removes tokens from the bag.
Two negative multipliers give a positive product.
activities.explanation: Tokens make each multiplication action easier to see.

activities.title: Understand the multiplication
activities.prompt: What does 4 × 2 mean in this lesson?
activities.explanation: Good choice. The multiplication repeats the same token action.

activities.title: Count the positive tokens
activities.prompt: The bag has ______ positive tokens after adding 2 positives 4 times.
activities.hint: Count all the tokens placed into the bag.
activities.explanation: You counted 2 positive tokens 4 times correctly.

activities.title: Match multipliers to their actions
activities.prompt: Match each multiplier description to the correct action.
activities.explanation: Great matching! The sign of each multiplier controls the token action.

activities.prompt: A helper puts 4 laddoos in each of 4 bags. How many laddoos are in all the bags?
activities.explanation: There are 4 groups of 4 laddoos, so 4 * 4 = 16 laddoos.

activities.prompt: After removing the positives, (–4) × 2 has a product of +8.
activities.explanation: After removing the positives, 8 negative tokens remain. The product is –8.

activities.prompt: A token model removes 2 negative tokens 3 times. How many positive tokens are there?
activities.explanation: Removing 2 negative tokens 3 times gives 2 * 3 positive tokens.

activities.prompt: A bag starts with 4 positive tokens. A positive multiplier adds 2 positive tokens 4 times. How many positive tokens are in the bag?
activities.explanation: The bag keeps its first 4 tokens and gains 2 * 4 tokens, giving 4 + 2 * 4 tokens.

activities.prompt: One token model adds 2 marbles 2 times. Another removes 3 marbles 4 times. How many more positive marbles does the first product have than the second, in marbles?
activities.explanation: The first product is 2 * 2 marbles. The second product is -(3 * 4) marbles, so the difference is 2 * 2 + 3 * 4 marbles.

lessons.title: Patterns and signs in integer multiplication

activities.prompt: Can you spot how integer multiplication changes when the multiplier moves backward?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Spot the multiplication patterns
activities.body: With a positive multiplicand, lowering the multiplier by 1 lowers the product by the multiplicand. With a negative multiplicand, lowering it by 1 increases the product by the multiplicand. It continues for negative multipliers. For any a, –1 × a equals a's opposite number, called the additive inverse. Changing both signs keeps the product's magnitude. Positive and negative integers make a negative product. Swapping the integers keeps the product.
keyPoints: Lowering the multiplier reveals a product pattern.
The sign rule tells us when a product is negative.
Integer multiplication is commutative.
activities.explanation: These patterns help you predict products and signs.

activities.prompt: What happens when the multiplicand is positive and the multiplier is lowered by 1?
options: The product lowers by the multiplicand.
The product rises by the multiplicand.
activities.explanation: Lowering the multiplier by 1 lowers the product by the multiplicand.

activities.prompt: Swapping the multiplier and multiplicand changes the product.
activities.explanation: Swapping the multiplier and multiplicand gives the same product.

activities.prompt: Match each starting situation with its result.
activities.explanation: Each result follows the multiplication rule for that situation.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to use the rule.
items: Call the result the additive inverse of a
activities.explanation: The rule starts with an integer and gives its additive inverse.

activities.prompt: Which statement about changing both signs is correct?
options: The product's magnitude stays the same.
activities.explanation: Changing the signs of the multiplier and multiplicand does not change the magnitude.

activities.prompt: The multiplication pattern stops when the multiplier becomes negative.
activities.explanation: The multiplication pattern continues when the multiplier becomes negative.

activities.prompt: Which equality shows that swapping the multiplier and multiplicand gives the same product?
activities.explanation: Swapping the multiplier and multiplicand gives the same product.

activities.prompt: A tray holds 5 laddoos and there are 4 trays. If the number of trays is lowered by 1, how many laddoos are on the trays?

activities.prompt: How did Brahmagupta change the way we think about negative numbers?

activities.title: Brahmagupta’s Rules
activities.body: Brahmagupta gave explicit rules for multiplication and division in 628 CE. He used fortune for positive values and debt for negative values. His rules covered positive and negative numbers. One rule says that the product or quotient of two debts is a fortune. These were the first explicit rules for multiplication and division of positive and negative numbers.
keyPoints: Fortune means a positive value.
Debt means a negative value.
The product or quotient of two debts is a fortune.
activities.explanation: These rules helped people work with positive and negative numbers.

activities.title: Fortune or Debt?
activities.prompt: What did Brahmagupta use for positive values?
activities.explanation: Brahmagupta used fortune for positive values.

activities.title: Match Each Idea

activities.prompt: Each packet has 5 laddoos, and there are 3 packets. How many laddoos are there in all?

activities.prompt: Two debts of 3 rupees and 3 rupees are multiplied. What signed amount in rupees is the product?

activities.prompt: Ravi owes 24 rupees, and Meena owes 2 rupees. Ravi's debt is divided by Meena's debt. What signed quotient in rupees results?
